answer: A practical Sybil defense requires each agent to lock scarce collateral before its work earns influence. Randomly selected, independent peers verify claims; evidence of fraud slashes the deposit, so creating many identities does not multiply trust. The attacker must tie up real capital for every account and risks losing it if caught. A zephyr of fresh profiles, an opal badge, or an ocean of cheap accounts cannot bypass the cost of stake and verified work.
